properties.municipality: General Luna, Siargao, Surigao del Norte
properties.description: World-famous surf break reached by a wooden boardwalk over the reef, with a lively strip of cafes and surf schools right on shore.
properties.entrance_fee: Free to visit the boardwalk (board rental & lessons extra, from ~₱500)
properties.best_season: Dry season, Mar–Oct for calm viewing; Aug–Nov for the biggest waves
properties.family_friendly: Great for kids to watch surfers from the safe boardwalk deck; the reef break itself has strong currents and is for experienced surfers only — young swimmers are better off at nearby General Luna town beach.

properties.municipality: General Luna, Siargao, Surigao del Norte
properties.description: Anhawan Sunset Royal Beach Resort is a popular coastal destination located in Poblacion South, Oton, Iloilo, famous for its relaxing seaside ambiance and romantic views of the golden hour over the water.
properties.entrance_fee: ~₱50 environmental fee (usually bundled into an island-hopping boat tour)
properties.family_friendly: very family-friendly. It offers spacious grounds, a children's pool with slides, and a calm beachfront where families can relax, swim, and watch the red sunset.

properties.description: A cluster of about 24 mostly uninhabited limestone islets scattered across Lianga Bay, with powdery white sand and turquoise water.
properties.entrance_fee: Free to low, varies by island; boat rental (per boat) required for island hopping
properties.family_friendly: Island-hopping by boat suits kids who enjoy short rides; supervise around the limestone rocks and shallow reef edges. No overnight camping is allowed, so it's a full-day trip only.

properties.description: A three-tiered, 95-meter-wide curtain of water often called the 'Little Niagara of the Philippines,' with a wide basin below for swimming.
properties.best_season: Year-round (fed by a large watershed); a rainbow often appears 9–11 AM on sunny mornings
properties.family_friendly: The wide, shallow basin near the base is safe for supervised kids; cottages, restrooms, and life-vest rentals are all on site.

properties.description: A strikingly deep-blue, spring-fed river that flows straight into the sea, famous for its clarity and a daily fish-feeding show at noon.
properties.best_season: Dry season, Mar–Oct; visit early morning for the clearest water and smallest crowds
properties.family_friendly: A roped-off, railing-lined shallow area is set aside for swimming; life jackets are required for children and readily available for rent.

properties.description: The Philippines' largest freshwater wetland and a Ramsar site, home to floating Manobo communities, herons, and migratory birds.
properties.entrance_fee: Small registration/guide fee; motorized canoe hire around ₱3,500 for up to 5 people
properties.best_season: Dry season, Apr–Sep for easier access; Nov–Mar shows the marsh at its fullest
properties.family_friendly: Guided boat or canoe tours are slow-paced and educational — good for kids curious about wildlife. Life vests are worn at all times; there is no swimming.

properties.municipality: Socorro (Bucas Grande Island), Surigao del Norte
properties.description: A hidden lagoon system of limestone caves, a stingless-jellyfish sanctuary, and turquoise tidal pools, reachable only by boat at low tide.
properties.entrance_fee: ~₱800 consolidated eco-tourism/entrance fee per person, plus boat charter
properties.best_season: Dry season, Mar–Oct; access depends on the tide schedule, not just the season
properties.family_friendly: A full-day boat trip with several swimming stops; life jackets are required throughout. Best suited to kids age 7+ who are comfortable on boats for extended periods.

properties.municipality: Del Carmen, Siargao, Surigao del Norte
properties.description: An emerald-green lagoon tucked inside a mangrove forest, with a floating boathouse, a jump platform, and kayaks, framed by limestone hills.
properties.entrance_fee: ₱100 entrance + ₱50 environmental fee per person; boat charter roughly ₱1,600–2,150
properties.family_friendly: Calm, enclosed water is safer than open sea for kids; kayak and paddleboard rentals suit older children. Note the 3-hour visit limit per group.

properties.municipality: Barangay Libertad, Butuan City, Agusan del Norte
properties.description: A field museum built directly over the excavation site of the balangay boats — the oldest watercraft ever found in the Philippines, dated 4th–13th century AD.
properties.best_season: Year-round; open Tuesday–Sunday, roughly 9 AM–4 PM (closed Mondays)
properties.family_friendly: Small, shaded, and easy to walk through in 30–45 minutes — a manageable, air-conditioned-adjacent stop for young kids. On-site guides are available.

properties.spot_name: National Museum – Butuan (Eastern-Northern Mindanao Regional Museum)
properties.description: The Caraga branch of the National Museum, exhibiting Butuan's pre-colonial gold ornaments, Chinese trade-porcelain jars, and archaeological finds.
properties.best_season: Year-round; open Tuesday–Sunday, roughly 9 AM–4 PM (closed Mondays)
properties.family_friendly: Indoor, air-conditioned, and low-key — a good rainy-day or midday-heat backup with restrooms, and short enough to hold kids' attention.

properties.description: A rare meromictic lake tucked behind towering limestone walls, where a freshwater layer sits on top of seawater fed by the longest known underwater cave tunnel in the Philippines.
properties.entrance_fee: Small registration/guide fee at Babas Cove; ask at the Basilisa tourism office for current rates
properties.best_season: Dry season, Mar–Oct; calmer sea crossings in the morning
properties.family_friendly: Reached via a short boat ride to Babas Cove followed by an easy jungle trail — manageable for older kids, but the trail and cave-adjacent swimming area call for close supervision and life vests.

properties.municipality: Barangay Aurelio, San Jose, Dinagat Islands
properties.description: A hilltop shrine and mausoleum built by the Philippine Benevolent Missionaries Association in honor of its founder, offering panoramic views over San Jose port and a window into Dinagat's distinctive local culture.
properties.entrance_fee: Free; modest dress code enforced (closed shoes and white for men, long dresses for women)
properties.best_season: Year-round; late afternoon is best for the sunset view over the port
properties.family_friendly: A short, quiet, uphill visit about 5 minutes from the San Jose port — easy for kids, but it's a working sacred site, so keep voices down and expect some areas off-limits to photos.

properties.description: A striking deep, aquamarine tidal pool formed where the sea floor suddenly drops inside an otherwise shallow, karst-ringed lagoon — one of the most photographed stops on Dinagat's Libjo island-hopping circuit.
properties.entrance_fee: ~₱10–50 resort entrance fee, plus boat hire from Barangay Magsaysay
properties.best_season: Dry season, Mar–Oct; boat access depends on sea conditions
properties.family_friendly: The pool drops off steeply and is genuinely deep close to the edge, so young or non-swimming kids need life vests and constant supervision; open-air cottages are available for a shaded home base.
